messages.content: What is the freezing point point of water at a pressure of 10 kPa?

message.content:
At a pressure of **10 kPa** (about 0.1 atm), pure water’s freezing (melting) point drops to roughly **–2 °C**.  
This is derived from the water phase diagram: as pressure decreases below atmospheric, the solid–liquid equilibrium line slopes downward, so the temperature at which ice melts (or water freezes) becomes lower. At 10 kPa the equilibrium temperature is about –2 °C (≈ 271 K).
